plan_notes: RECENCY: lead with outlet RSS / sitemap_news.xml feeds (rss_feeds_first) and filter by pubDate within the 72h window (since 2026-10-20T22:00Z). WebSearch site: queries tend to return evergreen pages - use WebSearch only to fill gaps, and verify every published time on the article page itself. 10-24 is a Saturday (KST): Friday 10-23 US/EU releases are the freshest primary documents; Friday KST Korean ministry releases also qualify.

SCOPE: follow sources.json categories[politics]._note - three axes only: (1) policy/regulation, (2) AI in elections & public opinion, (3) AI geopolitics. No AI-less general politics; if deleting AI from the headline leaves a standing story, drop it. Aim for spread across all three axes and regions.

BALANCE: 10-22 and 10-23 shipped zero geopolitics and zero copyright/liability rulings; 10-23 already has one Brazil TSE elections card and one Korea regulator card. Today the first 9 queries are geopolitics (export controls, MATCH Act/DUV, smuggling, China CAC, Gulf compute deals, sovereign AI, datacenter siting, Korea chip/sovereign AI) and the next two are copyright/liability courts - fill those axes first. Prefer decisions over essays/podcasts/analysis/lobbying-tally stories.

NEUTRALITY: non-partisan; report what was decided/filed/published; attribute contested claims to the named party; no horse-race or polling commentary (Brazil runoff is Oct 25, US midterms Nov 3). Prefer primary documents; primary doc and news report about it are ONE story.

DEDUP: do not resubmit anything in recently_published_do_not_resubmit. Follow-ups qualify only with a NEW ruling, filing, bill, executive order or official release (e.g. EO 14409 framework text due Oct 30, Newsom OES recommendations, Anthropic draft becoming an introduced bill, Commission/CMA action on Meta AI terms, actual DUV/BIS rule, Korea AI Basic Act amendment passing the National Assembly, finalized Korea FTC AI-washing guideline). Commentary/analysis/reactions on published events are dropped.

CROSS-SECTION: AI ad products / AI-washing ad claims (marketing), AI chip hardware launches (gadgets), medical AI approvals (medicine) belong elsewhere unless a government/regulator action is the news.
Paywalled/crawler-blocked majors (reuters, bloomberg, ft, wsj, nytimes, economist, foreignpolicy) are excluded - find the same decision on an allowed outlet or the primary source.
